items.title: CMA CGM’s Saadé concedes 2050 net zero target is out of reach
points: One of shipping’s most vocal proponents of decarbonisation has conceded that its 2050 net zero ambitions are unlikely to be realised, just days ahead of crucial environmental negotiations at the International Maritime Organization (IMO).
Speaking at the Assises de l’économie de la mer in Montpellier yesterday, CMA CGM chairman and CEO Rodolphe Saadé put the investment required to decarbonise global shipping at more than $1trn.
“We must be realistic: under current circumstances, we will not be able to meet our targets by 2050,” Saadé said.

The French shipping magnate cited geopolitical conflicts lengthening voyages and driving up operating costs, the absence of a unified international regulatory framework and the slow development of low-carbon fuels.
CMA CGM has already committed nearly $30bn to LNG- and methanol-powered newbuilds, with more than 200 dual-fuel vessels scheduled to be in its fleet by 2030.

items.title: Archbishop Emeritus of Guwahati Thomas Menamparampil dies at 90 in Hyderabad hospital
points: Guwahati, Archbishop Emeritus of Guwahati Reverend Thomas Menamparampil died at a hospital in Hyderabad on Wednesday following a brief illness.
The current Guwahati Archbishop, John Moolachira, said Menamparampil passed away at 5:40 am and described the death as an immense loss to the Church and all who experienced his pastoral care.
"Deeply saddened by the passing of Archbishop Emeritus of Guwahati, Most Rev.
Born on October 22, 1936, in Keralam's Pala, Menamparampil joined the Salesians of Don Bosco and was ordained a priest on May 2, 1965.
In 1992, Menamparampil became the first Bishop of Guwahati.
Following the elevation of the diocese, he was appointed the first archbishop of Guwahati in 1995, a post he held until his retirement in 2012.
In 2011, he was nominated for the Nobel Peace Prize in recognition of his sustained efforts to foster dialogue, harmony, and peace among conflicting ethnic and tribal communities in Northeast India.
Menamparampil received the Dr J Abdul Kalam World Peace Award in 2023 and the Peace Award in 2026.

items.title: Chartered Speed targets December IPO after Iran war disruption
points: Chartered Speed is targeting a public listing in December after ​cutting the size of its initial public offering and ⁠delaying earlier plans as the Iran war roiled capital markets.

Indian bus operator ‌Chartered Speed is targeting a public listing in December after ​cutting the size of its initial public offering and ⁠delaying earlier plans as the Iran war roiled capital markets, a company executive said.
The company is awaiting regulatory clearance for an addendum to its IPO documents ‌and expects approval by the first week of December, Whole-Time Director Sanyam Gandhi told Reuters.
The Iran war unsettled India's ‌IPO market this year, prompting some firms to delay or ‌resize ⁠offerings and the market regulator to temporarily ease rules ⁠on IPO timelines and offer sizes.

points: The Tamil Nadu government has constituted a four-member Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) to investigate a sexual harassment complaint filed by a woman bureaucrat against TVK MLA C Arul Vignesh, following a direction from the Madras High Court on Tuesday.

items.title: The U.S Navy Cruiser That Sailed Home Missing One-Third of Her Hull During WWII
points: Researchers onboard the Exploration Vessel Nautilus found the damaged bow of the Second World War Cruiser USS New Orleans (CA-32) on July 7, 2025, at a depth of about 675 m in Iron Bottom Sound close to Guadalcanal, Solomon Islands.

Led by the Ocean Exploration Trust (OET) during the Maritime Archaeology of Guadalcanal expedition, the uncrewed surface vessel DriX identified the wreck while mapping the seabed, after which an ROV was used to capture its images.
The USS New Orleans was saved by its crew after it suffered damage from a Japanese ‘long-lance’ torpedo during the battle of Tassafaronga on November 30, 1942.
The USS New Orleans was the lead ship of the New Orleans-class of the U.S Navy and the first seven such ships built for the US Navy in the 1930s.
The class represented the last cruisers constructed according to the specifications laid down by the 1922 Washington Naval Treaty, earning them the name Treaty Cruisers.

items.title: Relocation of wild elephants does not solve human-elephant conflict in Keralam’s Chinnakkanal, finds study
points: District Collector Dineshan Cheruvatt had constituted the panel in September to find ways to address the rising human-elephant conflicts in Chinnakkanal.
According to sources, the panel’s report noted that authorities previously translocated a tusker known as Arikomban from Chinnakkanal to reduce conflict.
“The removal of these two ‘problematic’ elephants did not alleviate human-elephant conflict in Chinnakkanal,” the report stated.

“This indicates that removal of elephants is not a solution to the human-elephant conflict in the landscape.” Instead, the panel recommended attaching a radio transmitter to any identified “problematic” elephant to monitor its movements.
According to the panel, though elephants frequently visit Mathikettan Shola National Park, a rapid habitat assessment revealed a shortage in food.
To reduce disturbances, the panel called for regulating high-intensity lighting at resorts in Chinnakkanal, specifically naming Mahindra Serene, Club Mahindra and Sterling resorts.

To ensure unimpeded elephant movement, the panel recommended removing fences around the Thachangari estate, which block passage from the Anayirankal reservoir to upper Suryanelli via the 60-acre shola.

points: Maimoona Mollah, a representative of People Against SIR, told The Hindu that an intimation letter had been sent to the Delhi Police regarding the march earlier this week.

On September 9, Amina Khatun, a resident of Cooch Behar’s Khatamari village, delivered a baby girl at Dinhata Sub-Divisional Hospital.

items.title: Shipping’s glass ceiling proves stubbornly resilient
points: Women are losing ground in key commercial and technical roles at maritime companies despite reporting greater inclusion in the workplace, according to the latest annual review from the Diversity Study Group (DSG).

The seventh edition of the Annual DEI in Maritime Review, which surveyed nearly 1,700 shore-based employees across 11 organisations, identifies a seemingly impenetrable glass ceiling at head of department level, where women account for just 14.6% of…
Female representation in technical and fleet management positions has fallen from 22.4% last year to 13.2%, while in commercial departments the proportion has dropped from 37.9% to 28.4%.
Female representation in IT has almost halved since 2023.
More encouragingly, over 90% of female respondents feel encouraged to contribute ideas for the first time, while 93% report having a supportive peer group.

Another recurring theme in the annual survey is what DSG describes as the “squeezed middle”, with mid-career employees expressing the greatest frustration over stalled careers, salary discrepancies, favouritism and management behaviour.

The CSC has emerged as a key regional security grouping of Indian Ocean littoral states, comprising India, Sri Lanka, the Maldives, Mauritius, Bangladesh, and Seychelles.
It has largely been focusing on maritime safety, counter-terrorism, and transnational security cooperation.
"The Colombo Security Conclave represents the intersection of our Neighbourhood First outlook and the MAHASAGAR vision," Mr. Doval said.

Last March, during his visit to Mauritius, Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced the vision MAHASAGAR, or 'Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions, for India's engagement with the Global South.
Mr. Doval said he was confident that the CSC will become an effective instrument in the Indian Ocean region to provide collective security and look after common interests.
